content: 1. Other orthopoxvirus infections include diseases such as cowpox and vaccinia. These are caused by viruses belonging to the Orthopoxvirus genus and can result in skin lesions and systemic symptoms. 2. Molluscum contagiosum is a viral infection caused by a poxvirus, leading to the development of small, raised, and typically painless lesions on the skin. 3. Exanthema subitum, also known as sixth disease, is caused by human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) or HHV-7. It is characterized by a sudden high fever followed by a distinctive rash. 4. Erythema infectiosum, commonly referred to as fifth disease, is caused by parvovirus B19. It presents with a slapped cheek rash on the face and may involve systemic symptoms such as fever and joint pain. 5. Enteroviral vesicular stomatitis with exanthem, including hand, foot, and mouth disease, is caused by coxsackieviruses or other enteroviruses. It is characterized by vesicular lesions on the hands, feet, and oral mucosa. 6. Enteroviral vesicular pharyngitis, also known as herpangina, is caused by enteroviruses and presents with vesicular lesions in the oropharynx, fever, and sore throat. 7. Other specified viral infections characterized by skin and mucous membrane lesions include conditions such as foot-and-mouth disease, which is caused by a picornavirus and primarily affects livestock but can occasionally infect humans. 8. Unspecified viral infections characterized by skin and mucous membrane lesions are those where the causative virus is not identified but present with similar clinical features. 9. Acute hepatitis A is a viral liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus (HAV), transmitted via the fecal-oral route, and characterized by jaundice, fatigue, and abdominal pain. 10. Acute hepatitis B is caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV), transmitted through blood and bodily fluids, and can lead to both acute and chronic liver disease. 11. Acute hepatitis C is caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV), primarily transmitted through blood. It often progresses to chronic infection and can result in liver cirrhosis or cancer. 12. Acute hepatitis E is caused by the hepatitis E virus (HEV), transmitted via contaminated water or food, and is particularly severe in pregnant women. 13. Chronic viral hepatitis refers to long-term liver inflammation caused by persistent viral infections, such as chronic hepatitis B or C. 14. Unspecified viral hepatitis includes cases where the specific viral cause of hepatitis is not determined. 15. HIV disease resulting in infectious and parasitic diseases includes complications such as mycobacterial infections, cytomegaloviral disease, candidiasis, and Pneumocystis pneumonia, among others. 16. HIV disease resulting in malignant neoplasms includes conditions such as Kaposi's sarcoma, Burkitt's lymphoma, and other non-Hodgkin's lymphomas, as well as other malignancies of lymphoid and hematopoietic tissues. 17. HIV disease resulting in other specified diseases includes complications such as HIV-associated encephalopathy, lymphoid interstitial pneumonitis, and wasting syndrome. 18. Acute HIV infection syndrome refers to the initial stage of HIV infection, characterized by flu-like symptoms and high viral replication. 19. HIV disease resulting in persistent generalized lymphadenopathy involves chronic swelling of lymph nodes due to immune system activation. 20. HIV disease resulting in hematological and immunological abnormalities includes conditions such as anemia, thrombocytopenia, and immune dysfunction not classified elsewhere. 21. Cytomegaloviral disease is caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) and can result in systemic or localized infections, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. 22. Mumps is a viral infection caused by the mumps virus, characterized by parotid gland swelling, fever, and potential complications such as orchitis or meningitis. 23. Infectious mononucleosis, caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), presents with fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, and fatigue. 24. Viral conjunctivitis is an inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by adenoviruses or other viruses, leading to redness, tearing, and irritation of the eyes. 25. Epidemic myalgia, also known as Bornholm disease, is caused by coxsackieviruses and presents with severe chest or abdominal pain and fever. 26. Ross River disease, caused by the Ross River virus, is characterized by polyarthritis, rash, and systemic symptoms such as fever and fatigue. 27. Viral carditis refers to inflammation of the heart muscle caused by viral infections, which can lead to myocarditis and cardiac dysfunction. 28. Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a severe respiratory illness caused by hantaviruses, characterized by fever, myalgia, and acute pulmonary edema. 29. Dermatophytosis includes fungal infections such as tinea barbae (beard ringworm), tinea capitis (scalp ringworm), tinea unguium (onychomycosis or nail fungus), tinea manuum (hand fungus), tinea pedis (athlete's foot), tinea corporis (ringworm of the body), tinea imbricata, and tinea cruris (jock itch). 30. Other superficial mycoses include conditions such as pityriasis versicolor, tinea nigra, white piedra, and black piedra, which affect the skin or hair. 31. Candidiasis includes infections such as oral thrush (candidal stomatitis) and pulmonary candidiasis, caused by Candida species, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.
